The Fourier transform that we used in this section is often called the Discrete Fourier Cosine Transform because it is defined using a basis $\ccal$ consisting of cosine functions. There is also a Fourier Sine Transform defined using a basis $\scal$ consisting of sine functions. For instance, in $\real^4$, the basis vectors of $\scal$ are $$ \begin{aligned} \vvec_1 = \left[\begin{array}{c} \sin\left(\frac{1\cdot1\pi}{8}\right) \\ \sin\left(\frac{3\cdot1\pi}{8}\right) \\ \sin\left(\frac{5\cdot1\pi}{8}\right) \\ \sin\left(\frac{7\cdot1\pi}{8}\right) \\ \end{array}\right], \amp \vvec_2 = \left[\begin{array}{c} \sin\left(\frac{1\cdot2\pi}{8}\right) \\ \sin\left(\frac{3\cdot2\pi}{8}\right) \\ \sin\left(\frac{5\cdot2\pi}{8}\right) \\ \sin\left(\frac{7\cdot2\pi}{8}\right) \\ \end{array}\right], \\ \\ \vvec_3 = \left[\begin{array}{c} \sin\left(\frac{1\cdot3\pi}{8}\right) \\ \sin\left(\frac{3\cdot3\pi}{8}\right) \\ \sin\left(\frac{5\cdot3\pi}{8}\right) \\ \sin\left(\frac{7\cdot3\pi}{8}\right) \\ \end{array}\right], \amp \vvec_4 = \left[\begin{array}{c} \sin\left(\frac{1\cdot4\pi}{8}\right) \\ \sin\left(\frac{3\cdot4\pi}{8}\right) \\ \sin\left(\frac{5\cdot4\pi}{8}\right) \\ \sin\left(\frac{7\cdot4\pi}{8}\right) \\ \end{array}\right]\text{.} \\ \end{aligned} $$ We can think of these vectors graphically, as shown in [fig-fourier-sine-basis].

The vectors $\vvec_1,\vvec_2,\vvec_3,\vvec_4$ that form the basis $\scal$.

The Sage cell below defines the matrix S whose columns are the vectors in the basis $\scal$ as well as the matrix C whose columns form the basis $\ccal$ used in the Fourier Cosine Transform.

In the $8\times8$ block of luminance values we considered in this section, the first column begins with the four entries 176, 181, 165, and 139, as seen in [fig-jpeg-block-luminance]. These form the vector $\xvec=\fourvec{176}{181}{165}{139}$. Find both $\coords{\xvec}{\scal}$ and $\coords{\xvec}{\ccal}$.

Write a sentence or two comparing the values for the Fourier Sine coefficients $\coords{\xvec}{\scal}$ and the Fourier Cosine coefficients $\coords{\xvec}{\ccal}$.

Suppose now that $\xvec=\fourvec{100}{100}{100}{100}$. Find the Fourier Sine coefficients $\coords{\xvec}{\scal}$ and the Fourier Cosine coefficients $\coords{\xvec}{\ccal}$.

Write a few sentences explaining why we use the Fourier Cosine Transform in the JPEG compression algorithm rather than the Fourier Sine Transform.
